newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle close mixed after new high.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle close mixed after new high.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed mixed after posting a new contract high in April earlier on further cash strength. Feeder cattle ended lower following weakness in deferred live cattle, traders said.

Live cattle closed 0.275 cent higher to 0.325 lower with April up most at 70.225 after posting a new contract high of 70.400 cents earlier. Feeder cattle ended 0.050 to 0.275 lower with March off the least at 68.675 cents.
April live cattle ran up to a new high for the sixth day in row following reports packers paid $69 per cwt for fed cattle in the southwest, traders said.

Futures then traded unevenly higher as profit taking and new commercial hedging entered the market at times. Commercials were on both sides of the market while funds bought. Reports of $70 cash cattle sales kept buying interest in the market. Profit taking again weighed on deferred contracts most of the day, they said.

Packers raised bids following the continued strong tone to boxed beef and competition for slaughter numbers. Heavy-weight choice boxed beef rose to $104.66 per cwt at noon, the highest price level since January 2, and this should keep demand strong for cash cattle, they said.

Cargill Investor Services sold April late but local buying and market-on-close orders kept prices firm. Lind-Waldock bought June. E.D.&F. Man, Refco and RBH were notable buyers early while R.J. O'Brien, RBH and LFG sold, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, commercials sold April 70 calls on the early rally. Later there was general buying of 68 puts and 70 to 72 calls. Commission houses sold Oct 66 puts, pit sources added.
Feeder cattle futures followed the lead of live cattle and moved up early before slipping late along with deferred live cattle positions, traders said.
Some pressure was also attributed to expectations of seasonally larger feeder supplies ahead. This also offset a slightly higher CME feeder cattle index and lower corn futures, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.05 at $69.01 per cwt.
Refco sold May early but bought late. Refco also spread long March/short May while LIT division of First Options took the other side. Dean Witter spread long September/short May, pit sources said.
